children: is in advanced discussions to acquire the San Francisco-based AI startup Decart as part of a $7.5B deal that could be announced as early as next week, The Financial Times reported on Saturday.
Founded in 2023 by three Israeli engineers, Moshe Shalev and brothers Dean and Orian Leitersdorf, Decart was an early adopter of Amazon’s
Trainium3 chips, which the e-commerce giant launched last year to rival Nvidia’s
The company’s main software product helps developers to alternate between different AI chips, a key competitive advantage at a time when the race to secure additional computing power is intensifying.
The talks to strike a deal valuing Decart at roughly 7.5B have reached the final stages, people familiar with the matter said, adding that an agreement with Amazon
could be finalized as soon as early next week, but discussions could still fall apart.
Decart was valued at $4B in May following a $300M funding round backed by a group of early-stage investors, including Sequoia Capital and Nvidia
. The company is also developing Lucy and Oasis world models, which can live edit video and create interactive virtual worlds.
